declared_limits.statement: Layer 1 checks syntactic FORM, not semantics. `fails_when:` is satisfied by the literal string `n/a`; `verify:` is satisfied by naming any file that resolves; a boundary-coverage tag is satisfied by a task whose entire body is `TODO.`. An artifact set carrying three of the six AC-7 defect classes therefore passes Layer 1 outright — see fixture `f-g-composed-semantic-bypass`. This is by architecture: semantics are Layer 2's charter. AC-7 is discharged by this disclosure plus Layer 2, NEVER by a claim that Layer 1 rejects the six classes. Do not state that Layer 1 alone gates dispatch.

`certificate_seal` and `section_seals` are TAMPER-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof. They carry no secret, so an editor who recomputes every seal after editing a section produces a self-consistent forgery. What they close is the defect actually observed: a hand-edited verdict surviving --verify with exit 0.

The reviewer-liveness anchor binds the INPUTS this program exposes, not the program itself. A caller who edits or copies the certifier, or replaces the ai-ask.sh sitting beside it, is modifying the program rather than supplying an input; that is the ENV-1 class and is CI's / 5.2.9's guarantee, not a stage acceptance criterion. `inputs.anchor.certifier_sha256` is recorded so such a certificate is at least identifiable.

A `verify:` token that resolves to an executable on PATH is bound BY NAME only. Hashing an interpreter would make determinism_key machine-specific and AC-8 unprovable across clones. Targets that resolve to a file under the artifact root ARE content-bound, and those are the material preconditions.

The recorded reviewer-response fixtures (`fixtures/_replay/`) prove the Layer-2 PARSING and AGGREGATION path — verdict extraction, finding extraction, threshold arithmetic, and the REJECT->final_gate:FAIL edge — offline and without credentials. They prove NOTHING about a live reviewer's judgement quality, and a live panel remains non-deterministic (see AC-8 scoping).

`determinism_key` is claimed for LAYER 1 AND the inputs and observations this certificate records — NOT for the artifact hashes alone. Two sources of non-determinism are disclosed. (1) LAYER 1: `L1-11` reads live filesystem state, so the SAME five artifact hashes can yield PASS and then FAIL when the evidence a `verify:` clause names changes. That is inherent to observing the tree and is NOT a defect; it is made attributable rather than eliminated — the observation is recorded in `traceability.observed_state`, folded into `determinism_key`, and re-compared by --verify, so the two verdicts carry two different keys. (2) LAYER 2: a live reviewer panel is non-deterministic, so `final_gate` is not a deterministic function of the recorded inputs whenever Layer 2 executes live.

AC-4's downstream-leakage detector is EXACT-LINE and length-bounded: it searches the reviewer payload for whole stripped lines of the downstream artifacts that are at least 40 characters long and do not start with '#' (`probe_lines`, `[p for p in probes if p in payload]`). CEILING: a payload that re-wraps, truncates, paraphrases or summarises the spec/plan/test/done text leaks the same intent and is NOT detected, and `attestation_valid` would still be true because bytes were captured and probes existed. What is detected is verbatim inclusion, which is the defect actually observed. `probe_lines_checked` and `payload_bytes` are recorded so a reader can see the size of the comparison rather than infer it.

--verify RECONCILES every caller-supplied source against the certificate's own sealed record before comparing anything: the artifact root's realpath, the five artifact source paths and sections, which of them were overridden by a --*-file flag, the boundary in force and where it came from, the coverage declaration, and the epic/stage identity. A certificate is therefore verifiable ONLY against the tree it was certified in: pointing --verify at a pristine copy, or substituting a source with --spec-file, is reported as a provenance mismatch and exits 1 — it is NOT an operator convenience, because `dispatch_allowed` must never depend on an unchecked caller input. CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than discovered: a certificate does not verify from a fresh clone at a different absolute path; re-certify there instead. NOT reconciled, because --verify does not re-run Layer 2 and so cannot be moved by them: the reviewer invoker, the reviewer timeout and `inputs.verdict_affecting.reviewer_environment`.

The reviewer invoker is executed with the FULL inherited environment (only HOME is overridden, to keep credential discovery inside the isolated cwd). `inputs.verdict_affecting.reviewer_environment` records every variable the invoker chain was READ to consume — model selection, token budget, retry and timeout behaviour, and the credential source — enumerated by inspecting ai-ask.sh / ai-call-gemini.sh / ai-certify-semantic-reviewer.sh / ai-common.sh at the line numbers cited in this certifier's LAYER2_ENV_INPUTS table. API keys are recorded as a truncated sha256 FINGERPRINT, never verbatim, so the auth identity actually used is identifiable (ENV-2) without the certificate carrying a secret. CEILING: the enumeration is a code-inspection snapshot. A future edit to the invoker chain that reads a variable not in that table would move a Layer-2 outcome unrecorded, and PATH / interpreter substitution is outside it entirely — that is the ENV-1 class, which is CI's / 5.2.9's guarantee and not a stage acceptance criterion.

CLAUDE_BIN.consumed_by: semantic reviewer judge binary — ai-certify-semantic-reviewer.sh:24 selects the claude CLI; the review SCRIPT's content is bound separately via verdict_affecting.semantic_invoker_sha256

AI_ENGINE_ROOT.consumed_by: the only credential source — ai-common.sh:51-53 -> $AI_ENGINE_ROOT/.ai/config/api_keys.conf; bound by that file's sha256, never by its absolute path

findings: **Intent softening on RR-5 (defensible, but name it):** ROADMAP RR-5 requires "Every displayed KPI value equals the frozen **validated** snapshot" (source WORK-AC-19/WORK-DEC-7); spec AC-5 substitutes "frozen **synthetic IS_DEMO** snapshot." This is licensed by WORK-BR-12 + the spec's Ambiguity Rule and correctly satisfies WORK-AC-19's negative constraint (never present 219/139 as authoritative). But WORK-AC-4's *positive* half — "retains validated portfolio KPI counts" — is deferred to a later data-prep validation with no visible stage owning the swap-in. Acceptable for this stage; flagged as the one candidate for lost intent.

**Phantom AC references in the plan (minor):** the numbered Implementation Steps cite AC-6…AC-11 (`plan.md` lines 35, 41, 47, 53, 60, 64, 84) but the spec defines only AC-1…AC-5. Stale numbering from an earlier revision. The anchored Plan Tasks (T-1…T-5) and traceability map correctly to AC-1…AC-5, so a Builder is not blocked, but the "Why" annotations are misleading.

**Two blocking checklist items have no mechanical check (Checklist-Preservation gap):** spec's *mandatory* checklist requires "No raw hex colors in components (tokens only)" and "No live LLM / Assessment / Simulate / Ask-AI code in `src/`," but neither `verify.sh` nor any TEST-n covers them (confirmed: no `hex`/`llm`/`assessment` matches in verify.sh). They rely on manual review, which contradicts the no-human-in-loop premise.

Tests TEST-1..TEST-4 have real, non-vacuous negative controls (SceneLayer omitted / filter no-op / new-SceneView-per-switch / reload-on-degrade), and verify.sh AC-3 (exactly one `new SceneView`, no `location.reload|href=`) is a genuinely non-trivial structural proof. Done-criteria are observable via `verify.sh`. No Builder-forcing ambiguity beyond the two authored Open Questions (polygon pick, portfolio size), both bounded by the Ambiguity Rule.

lens_b_findings:
**Central invariant is mechanically vacuous for the exact literals it names (lead finding):** INV-no-mockup-numbers / AC-5 forbid hard-coding "139 / 219 / AED 85B." A Builder can write `
219
` in `KpiStrip.tsx` and: `verify.sh` `check_data` passes (no `B` token in "219"), TEST-5 *as specified* passes (it only asserts `AED B` absence + provenance + IS_DEMO + attribution — it never asserts KPI values are computed), so AC-5 goes GREEN while the invariant is violated with the precise screenshot count (WORK-AC-19/WORK-DEC-7) the stage exists to protect. The guard *deliberately* exempts bare 139/219 (spec line 290) to avoid coordinate/id false positives — but nothing replaces that coverage. **Fix:** TEST-5 must assert KPI/count values are imported from the aggregate module (or forbid numeric JSX literals in `src/ui/Kpi*`); "reviewed manually" (plan line 93) is not a valid guard here.

**Documented guard ≠ implemented guard, plus false-positive risk:** spec (lines 287–290) documents a guard *scoped to `src/ui/`* matching only `AED 85B|85B`; `verify.sh:36` implements *all of `src/`* matching *any* `AED <n>B` **or** `\b<n>B\b`. A Builder who writes the narrow spec-documented guard will be failed by the broad one. The broad pattern also risks false positives on legitimate content (a "1.42B" data label, or an uppercase 3-digit hex like `#12B` in `tokens.css`), which would block a correct implementation.

No authorization/IDOR/money/state-transition/concurrency surface applies — read-only frozen demo dataset, no backend, no tenancy (Risk Surface: none). Confirmed against the contract; no such path constructible.

AOI-swap integrity (the stage core invariant) is well-fenced: the "SceneView constructed exactly once + no full-reload" pair is enforced both in `verify.sh` AC-3 and TEST-3 with an explicit `fails_when`. No green-while-absent path here.

questions.independent_advisory: INDEPENDENT ROADMAP REVIEW. You are shown ONE artifact: a roadmap stage entry. You are deliberately NOT shown the spec, plan, tests or done-criteria. State, as a numbered list, exactly what this stage must deliver, and what would constitute lost intent if a downstream spec omitted it. End with '## Verdict: PASS' if the roadmap entry is itself intelligible and actionable, 'CONCERN' if ambiguous, 'REJECT' if it cannot be acted on.
questions.combined_two_lens:
TWO-LENS SEMANTIC REVIEW (pre-implementation). Produce TWO independent, separately-verdicted lenses over the SAME grounded inspection of THIS repo. Do NOT let one overall narrative substitute for the two lens results. Complete Lens A fully, THEN RESET posture for Lens B — Lens B is an adversary, not a continuation of Lens A. Apply each check only when relevant to this stage; do not force domain-specific checks that do not apply.

## Lens A — Builder Readiness
Judge ONLY whether a Builder with no human in the loop could DELIVER this stage from these artifacts (no implementation exists yet). Answer, citing the artifact: (1) does the Spec preserve roadmap intent — any LOST intent or UNINTENDED SCOPE EXPANSION? (2) does each Plan task genuinely satisfy the criterion it claims? (3) do the Tests PROVE behaviour or merely execute code? (4) name a concrete scenario where the tests stay GREEN while the required behaviour is ABSENT (or say you cannot construct one); (5) would the Done-Criteria demonstrate success post-implementation? A traceability matrix is supplied — judge it, do not reconstruct it; (6) any ambiguity that would force the Builder to INVENT? Emit EXACTLY:
## Lens A Verdict: PASS|CONCERN|REJECT
#### Lens A Findings
(one '- ' bullet each; '- none' if empty)

## Lens B — Hostile Implementation Audit
RESET your posture: assume that following this package LITERALLY could still produce a WRONG system, and it is your job to prove it against the ACTUAL repository. Hunt, citing file:line: GROUNDING (do every named symbol / DTO field / method / enum value / route / config key EXIST with the claimed semantics?); contract/schema mismatch; authorization / IDOR / cross-tenant / cross-branch access; money, discount, commission, refund, rounding, settlement integrity where applicable; invalid or incomplete state transitions; CONCURRENCY, REPLAY and IDEMPOTENCY problems (races, double-apply, non-atomic read-modify-write); uniqueness / collision assumptions; read-only vs write boundary violations; determinism; stale-data / race behaviour; failure/retry semantics; any path where tests stay GREEN while required behaviour is absent; any implementation that technically satisfies the written package while violating its intended behaviour. For each, exhibit the concrete failing path (inputs -> wrong result, file:line) or state you could not construct one. Emit EXACTLY:
## Lens B Verdict: PASS|CONCERN|REJECT
#### Lens B Findings
(one '- ' bullet each; '- none' if empty)

## Overall
Then emit the single final overall verdict = the WORSE of Lens A and Lens B (PASS only if BOTH are PASS).
